# Independent audit: supporting-facet transport and incoming mass



Source: `candidate c0611f2da2e55fa1`.
Verifier: `supporting computation verify_supporting_facet_incoming_mass_coherent.py`.


read. The verifier reran successfully with **53 exact checks**.

## 1. Restriction and its exact correction

At a source point on a supporting hyperplane, its nonnegative target
support slack has conditional expectation zero by the physical
martingale identity. It therefore vanishes almost surely in that
row. Thus source rows on F stay on F, including rows at intersections
of several ambient facets. Restricting rows gives a target submeasure
eta_F^0 of eta|_F; the missing submeasure is exactly the target law
of rows arriving from outside F. Taking masses gives

    eta(F)-nu(F) = incoming mass >= 0.

Zero correction is equivalent to full target restriction, not merely
a sufficient condition. The added diagonal coupling of the incoming
submeasure gives the balanced convex-order statement with equal mass
and all affine moments. Without this correction, Jensen followed by
the target-submeasure inequality is valid for nonnegative convex
tests only. The source correctly keeps this distinction for signed
convex tests. All sets are Borel and supporting slack is bounded on
the fixed compact polytope.

## 2. Normal marks, straightening, and Hausdorff measures

At a fixed integer base, F_p is the exposed u-face of the positive
full-dimensional fiber K_p. If it has dimension d-1, its relative
interior has the unique own-fiber outward normal u; all intersections
with distinct own-fiber facet directions are boundary-null. If it
has smaller dimension, it is also boundary-null. When several ambient
facets induce the same own-fiber facet, the own normal and measure
are still single-valued almost everywhere, so no multiplicity is
introduced. For d=1 the nonempty exposed face is one endpoint with
its correct signed normal and counting mass one.

Consequently the physical restriction eta|_F has constant normal u
almost everywhere. The affine parametrization

    Psi(z,t)=(z,Et+(b-a.z)u)

is a bijection onto the supporting hyperplane, leaves base coordinates
unchanged, and is an isometry in t at each fixed base. The discrete
fiber target is exactly the sum of H_(d-1) on the reduced fibers;
there is no slope factor in it. The reduced body's projection has
the same actual integer bases, so its full base trace is lattice-
complete. If eta(F)>0, at least one reduced fiber has dimension d-1,
making this same measure the intrinsic Hausdorff measure of the
reduced mixed trace. Lower-dimensional reduced fibers are null.

The separately stated ambient Jacobian is sqrt(1+|a|^2): base tangent
vectors have Gram matrix I+aa^T, are orthogonal to the isometric
t-vectors, and the latter have identity Gram matrix. The n-dimensional
projection coarea Jacobian on the facet tangent space is its
reciprocal. These statements include n=0 and d=1 with their stated
zero-dimensional conventions. Neither factor is inserted into the
discrete fiber sum.

## 3. Source law and cap traces

Pullback by an affine bijection preserves conditional barycenters,
mass equality, and every affine moment. Thus the corrected convex
order pulls back exactly as stated. Absolute-continuity densities
are composed with Psi without another Jacobian because the target
measure itself has already been pulled back fiberwise.

Substitution into an arbitrary ambient cap gives the displayed base
coefficient c-(v.u)a, continuous coefficient E^T v, and threshold
b_j-(v.u)b. This retains every oblique direction. A zero full normal
produces the whole reduced affine space or the empty set, while a
zero continuous component alone may still produce a nontrivial
pure-base halfspace. The source retains original allocation values
on positive-measure boundary coincidences rather than replacing them
by a closed indicator. The transversality qualification for obtaining
ordinary indicator densities is therefore necessary and present.

Even in the zero-incoming case the reduced target is a volume law
on the reduced fibers, and the source is its inherited cap-allocation
density. It is not the boundary measure/stress of the reduced body.
Original bulk cap budgets are not equated with reduced facet volumes.
The proof correctly draws no recursive OC induction from this law.

## 4. Unique ownership sufficient condition

Every measured own-fiber boundary point lies on at least one
nonvertical ambient facet. Under the stated almost-everywhere unique
ownership hypothesis, assign that facet as its label. Absolute
continuity gives the same property for the source. Source rows stay
on their labeled supporting facet, and target uniqueness makes their
target label identical. Hence no row crosses labels and every incoming
correction is zero. Vertical facets may contain whole fibers, but do
not provide a nonzero own-fiber normal; the proof does not confuse
them with nonvertical owners. The hypothesis is not assumed to hold
in general.

## 5. Exact positive-density counterexample

The five upper points have heights 0,1,2,1,0. Each upper own-fiber
facet has area one after any unit-cube padding. The displayed source
densities are positive and sum to five. The rows at bases 1 and 3
send masses (1/4,1,1/4), total 3/2, along their respective affine
upper edge. Their physical barycenters, after division by 3/2, are
exactly the middle source point. All other upper rows are diagonal.
Every target upper density is one, and the continuous normal and
the padded coordinates remain unchanged.

At either upper ambient facet the target restriction has mass three
and the raw source restriction has mass 11/4. Incoming mass 1/4
arrives at the shared base-two own-fiber facet from the other side.
All source rows already on the selected facet stay there. Thus the
correction is exactly the stated quarter-area law at base two, and
adding it gives matching mass and physical moments. The unchanged
other boundary pieces only meet the upper facets on boundary-null
sets, so they introduce no hidden additional mass, for every d>=1.

The example genuinely has positive source density everywhere on the
actual boundary, full unweighted target, and normal-preserving physical
martingale transport, yet neither upper raw restriction is balanced.
It proves precisely the asserted incoming-mass obstruction, without
claiming minimizing cap stress or contradicting the corrected law.

## Conclusion

Incoming correction, intrinsic measure identity, all Jacobians and
boundary allocation branches are tracked correctly. The reduced law
is a balanced lower-dimensional volume-source transport statement;
it supplies no recursive boundary-stress or bulk-budget assertion.
